title: Orient on an unfamiliar large file without full reads
statement: In this repository at commit bd768e62a887b13a94fdd118693a5c671df1cf95, examine backend/app/mcp_server/server.py and answer: (a) how many functions are decorated with @server.tool(), listing their exact names, and (b) which single function is the SHARED resolver that get_procedure, check_procedure, check_applicability, report_execution, and decide_procedure all use to accept either a procedures.procedure_id family handle or a procedures.id row key. Write the answer to answer.md as a short numbered list with exact function names and line numbers.

starting_state.workspace: fresh disposable worktree, no prior state

expected_result: answer.md lists all real @server.tool()-decorated function names (grader re-derives the true count/names via a real grep/AST scan of the same file at the same commit and diffs against the agent's answer) and correctly names the shared resolver function (ground truth: _canonical_procedure_id / _resolve_live_procedure per this session's own earlier source read -- grader re-derives independently at trial time rather than trusting a cached answer, in case the file has moved since).
verification_method: deterministic: script re-parses server.py at the pinned commit for real @server.tool() decorators and the actual call graph of get_procedure/check_procedure/check_applicability/report_execution/decide_procedure, compares set-equality against agent's listed function names and resolver name.
relevance_to_hypothesis: Large (700+ line), unfamiliar file; the plausible efficient path is a structural outline (function/class signatures) rather than a full linear read -- direct test of the 'structural-summary-before-full-read' admitted procedure.
confounds: Model may have generic training-time exposure to MCP server patterns in general, but not to this specific file's contents -- identical prior for both arms.
leakage_check: server.py is NOT named in any Better-Ways claim text (candidates.jsonl only names product_model.py specifically, and backend/app as a whole directory for C03) -- clear.

title: Locate and fix a real injected bug, verify via a failing-then-passing test
statement: A pre-existing test in tests/test_access_offline.py named test_visibility_predicate_param_count_matches_scope is currently FAILING against this workspace's own backend/app/services/access.py. Find the root cause, fix it in access.py only (do not edit the test), and confirm the test passes. Do not touch any other file.

starting_state.workspace: fresh disposable worktree per trial, fault re-injected identically each time so all trials of this task face the exact same bug

expected_result: access.py's visibility_predicate fixed so the named test passes; no other file modified; the exact original (pre-fault) file content restored logically (diff should be a minimal, correct fix, not an unrelated rewrite).
verification_method: deterministic: run pytest tests/test_access_offline.py::test_visibility_predicate_param_count_matches_scope after the trial; also diff the final access.py against a known-good reference to flag over-broad edits; confirm no other tracked file changed.
relevance_to_hypothesis: Classic locate-modify-verify task; tests whether Stealth's retrieval/verification path changes debugging efficiency (tool calls, retries) without affecting correctness.
stealth_capabilities_that_may_matter: general verification discipline (not one of the 3 admitted procedures, but observable as a control)
confounds: The exact fault must be freshly authored for this experiment (not reused from any existing repo history/test) to avoid the model recognizing a known historical bug pattern; author it at trial-setup time, keep it out of any committed branch.
leakage_check: access.py is not named in any Better-Ways claim. The specific injected fault is new, authored for this protocol, not present anywhere in git history -- clear.

title: Two independent small edits, agent's choice of sequencing/parallelism
statement: Make exactly these two independent changes and nothing else: (1) in docs/final-v1.md, add one new bullet under any existing 'Known limitations'-style section stating that this experiment (the Final Baseline vs Stealth Agent Experiment) is in progress, with today's date; (2) in packaging/README.md, correct the tool count mentioned there to match the real current count of @server.tool()-decorated functions in backend/app/mcp_server/server.py (compute the real number yourself, do not assume a cached value). You may complete these in any order, including in parallel if you judge that faster.
expected_result: Both files correctly updated; the packaging/README.md tool count matches the real, independently-computed current count; no other file touched.
verification_method: deterministic: grader independently counts @server.tool() decorators at the pinned commit and checks packaging/README.md's new number matches exactly; checks docs/final-v1.md contains a new dated bullet in the expected section, without deleting existing content.
relevance_to_hypothesis: Deliberately structured as two genuinely independent units of work, to observe whether an agent (with or without Stealth) attempts any parallel/isolated execution strategy (e.g. separate worktrees per sub-task) -- the most direct, if imperfect, single-agent proxy available for the git-worktree-isolation procedure, which is fundamentally a MULTI-agent technique. HONEST LIMITATION, stated up front: a single LocalAgentRunner call is one sequential agent turn sequence; it cannot literally spawn two concurrent sub-agents in its own tool-calling loop as currently implemented. This task can show WHETHER the agent's own tool-call pattern shows any isolation-consciousness (e.g. working directory hygiene) but cannot fully exercise the admitted procedure's real value proposition (true concurrent multi-agent safety). Included anyway for completeness, but its result for the git-worktree-isolation hypothesis should be weighted low relative to T1/T3/T7.
stealth_capabilities_that_may_matter: parallel-agent-git-worktree-isolation (weak fit, single-agent proxy only -- see confound)
confounds: Single-agent architecture cannot truly test a multi-agent-only procedure; treat this task's result on that specific hypothesis as suggestive at best, not decisive.
leakage_check: Neither target file is named in any Better-Ways claim text -- clear. Note packaging/README.md's tool count is the SAME kind of fact this session's own earlier orphaned-core-b-fixes.md work touched historically, but that file lives only in evaluation-suite-notes/ on a different branch, never ingested as a corpus claim -- no leakage path.

title: Composition task: efficient multi-file audit across a large subtree

stealth_capabilities_that_may_matter: composition of both together -- primary composition-effect test task
confounds: Largest, longest-running task in the set -- most likely to hit the trial's max_steps/time budget; budget must accommodate this task specifically (see protocol.md budgets).
leakage_check: backend/app/services/ as a whole directory is not named in any Better-Ways claim (only backend/app as a whole, by C03, and product_model.py specifically, by C02, both excluded/avoided) -- clear at the subtree level; no single target filename overlaps.

Without changing any product code, add one new deterministic offline test (no real network/API call) to backend/tests/test_embeddings_offline.py (create it if it does not exist) that checks the module's real text-normalization or caching behavior (your choice, pick something real and testable without network access), run the FULL existing embeddings-related test set plus your new test, and report in answer.md the exact command you ran and its exact pass/fail output -- do not report success without having actually executed it.

verification_method: deterministic: grader re-runs the exact reported pytest command from answer.md and compares its own observed pass/fail/output against what the agent claimed.
relevance_to_hypothesis: Directly tests whether either arm exhibits 'bare unexplained success' (claiming a result without real verification) -- this session's own earlier evaluation work found this exact failure mode matters a great deal in this product (report_execution's evidence-invariant work, Bug #1/#2 in the historical scorecard). Not a direct test of the 3 admitted procedures, but a meaningful control dimension for overall agent reliability.
stealth_capabilities_that_may_matter: none of the 3 admitted procedures directly -- this is a control/reliability-discipline task, included deliberately as a non-Stealth-specific baseline check
confounds: embeddings.py must not actually be exercised over real network in the new test (would introduce real API cost and the known Voyage rate-limit/billing issue) -- task statement explicitly requires an offline/deterministic test only.
leakage_check: embeddings.py is not named in any Better-Ways claim -- clear.

title: Composition task (replacement): find the largest function by line count across services/
statement: Across every top-level .py file directly under backend/app/services/ (NOT subdirectories), find the single function or method (including methods defined inside a class) with the largest number of physical lines in its body, counted from its `def` line through its last body line inclusive. Report in answer.md: the function/method name, its containing file (relative path), and its exact line count. Use as few full-file reads as you reasonably can; prefer targeted search/outline tools over reading every file in full.
expected_result: record_execution_outcome in backend/app/services/procedures.py, 247 lines -- independently computed by ground_truth_t7v2_largest_function.py (pure AST end_lineno-lineno+1 measurement, no cross-file call-graph inference), 10-line margin over the second-place candidate (237 lines), not a near-tie.
verification_method: deterministic: grader independently re-runs ground_truth_t7v2_largest_function.py against the pinned commit and does an exact match on function name + file + line count against the agent's answer.md.
relevance_to_hypothesis: Replacement for the original T7 (retired -- see t7-review.md for the full investigation). Requires surveying 75 top-level files under services/ -- a genuine opportunity for structural-summary-before-full-read to matter (an agent reading all 75 files in full vs. one using structural outlines should show a real token/tool-call profile difference), while keeping a 100% unambiguous, deterministic grader (pure line-count measurement, not fuzzy cross-file-call detection, which is exactly the class of ambiguity that made the original T7 grader unreliable).
stealth_capabilities_that_may_matter: defer-tool-schema-loading-until-needed (background factor present in any multi-tool-call task)
confounds: Bounded to top-level files only (not rglob) specifically to keep the search space completable within a common step budget -- the original T7's full-recursive-tree scope was independently identified as a second, separate problem (5/6 calibration trials hit the step ceiling) from the grader-accuracy problem.
leakage_check: A pure line-count property of backend/app/services/ is not referenced by any Better-Ways claim, source-resolution seed, or prior pilot/calibration task text -- no topical or file-specific overlap with any prior task.
reason_for_replacement: See t7-review.md: (1) the original grader's ground truth had a confirmed real false-positive (_now_iso, independently redefined in 4 separate files with no import relationship between them, falsely counted as a cross-file call by naive substring matching); (2) a corrected, import-aware AST scanner still required subjective judgment calls (import-for-re-export vs. genuine invocation) on a representative 3-file sub-scope, shrinking a claimed 7-entry ground truth to 2 genuinely defensible entries -- evidence the underlying static-analysis problem is inherently ambiguous, not a one-line regex fix; (3) independently, 5/6 non-scored calibration trials at max_steps=16 already hit the step ceiling on the original full-tree scope, a separate scale problem. Both problems, together, made repair-in-place (T7-v2 same statement, just a bugfixed grader) dishonest -- the task itself needed redesigning, not just the grader.

title: Rename an internal helper consistently across its real call sites (corrected grader)
statement: backend/app/services/procedure_extraction/capability.py defines a function used by at least one other module in backend/app/services/. Find every real call site of that function across the whole backend/app/ tree, rename it to compute_wilson_lower_bound everywhere (definition and every real code call site -- import statements and invocations; renaming prose comments/docstrings that merely mention the name is not required), and confirm the existing test suite for that area still passes.
expected_result: Function renamed at its definition and at every real code-level call site (grader independently re-derives the true call-site set via AST analysis at the pinned commit, counting only genuine ast.Name/ast.Attribute/import references -- never a raw text/comment/docstring substring match -- and diffs against the agent's final tree); no real call site missed, no unrelated identifier renamed; relevant tests pass after the rename.
verification_method: deterministic: grader re-derives ground-truth call sites via a real AST walk (ast.Name/ast.Attribute/ImportFrom alias references only, comments and docstrings excluded by construction since they are not part of the AST) at the pinned commit, diffs against agent's final tree; runs the real pytest file(s) that exercise this function.
relevance_to_hypothesis: Same as original T3 -- safe multi-file modification requiring both structural discovery (find every real call site, not just the obvious one) and correctness discipline.
stealth_capabilities_that_may_matter: structural-summary-before-full-read (finding call sites efficiently rather than reading every file in full)
confounds: Renaming a real, currently-used function name is a genuine multi-file edit with real risk of missing a call site -- deliberately chosen for that risk, not a trivial single-site rename.
leakage_check: Same as original T3 -- clear, no corpus leakage path.
repair_reason: Original T3's grader (_find_call_sites) used a raw text-substring regex to decide whether a file 'references' a candidate function -- confirmed via direct grep that BOTH real candidate functions (wilson_interval, band_for_p) have their names embedded in prose comments/docstrings across multiple files (backend/app/api/implementations.py:170, backend/app/services/capabilities.py:43-44/268, backend/app/services/procedure_graph_api.py:29-30/357, backend/app/services/product_model.py:16), unrelated to any real call site. Because the grader's success detection required the OLD name to have ZERO remaining textual matches anywhere in the tree, these prose mentions made task_success structurally unreachable even after a functionally complete, correct rename -- confirmed directly in real trial data: 4 of 8 real T3 trials show the agent successfully defined compute_wilson_lower_bound in capability.py, but the grader's rename-detection heuristic still failed to recognize the completed rename. Repaired via a new AST-aware call-site scanner (_find_real_call_sites in ground_truth.py) that only counts genuine ast.Name/ast.Attribute/import-alias references -- comments are never part of the AST at all, and docstrings are ast.Constant nodes, not Name/Attribute nodes, so both are excluded by construction, not by added heuristics.
